headline: The NAD+
question.
dek: NAD+ drips and injections are sold for aging. The largest trial of a related pill went the wrong way.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Oct 31, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: Largest trial
glance.line: NOPARK, 410 people with Parkinson’s: disease scores worsened more on oral NR than placebo.

glance.label: Not approved
glance.line: NAD+, NR, glutathione, MOTS-c and Epitalon: none is FDA approved for any use.

glance.label: Banned in sport
glance.line: MOTS-c is named under S4.4.1. NAD+, NR, metformin and Epitalon are not named.

summary: [[/nad|NAD+]] is a coenzyme every cell uses, and injections and nasal sprays of it are sold for aging. Neither form is FDA approved. The human evidence for injected NAD+ is one pilot infusion study in 11 healthy men, a chart review of 14 clinic clients and two Chinese trials of a hospital NAD+ injection for heart disease, not aging. We found no published human study of NAD+ nasal spray.

Its relative [[/nicotinamide-riboside|nicotinamide riboside]] (NR), a form of vitamin B3 the body turns into NAD+, has been tested in many randomized trials by mouth. It raises NAD+ in the blood, but effects on health have been small, mixed or absent. The largest, NOPARK, gave NR or placebo for 52 weeks to 410 people with early Parkinson’s disease, and outcomes were worse on NR. NR is sold as a supplement; no NR injection is FDA approved.

[[/metformin|Metformin]] is approved for type 2 diabetes; use for aging is off-label, and the proposed TAME aging trial has no registry record we could find. [[/mots-c|MOTS-c]] has no published study in people, and WADA bans it at all times. For [[/epitalon|Epitalon]], FDA found three studies that gave it to people. HHS now allows both to be compounded under set conditions, which is not approval. [[/ghk-cu|GHK-Cu]] and [[/sermorelin|sermorelin]] also sit in this lane, with no human study measuring longevity.

[[/glutathione|Glutathione]] injections raise a quality problem. In August 2026 FDA said at least 30 patients had adverse events after IV glutathione made from supplement-grade ingredient from one supplier, and it had warned about the same risk in 2019. None of these treatments has been shown to slow aging in people.

pull.quote: The glutathione was labeled as dietary supplement grade, which is not an appropriate ingredient to make injectable drugs.

excerpts.quote: FDA is aware of reports of at least 30 patients who experienced adverse events following the administration of intravenous (IV) glutathione alone or in combination with other ingredients.
excerpts.source: FDA, reminder to compounders on supplement-grade glutathione

excerpts.quote: FDA received a report concerning seven patients who received an injectable drug compounded with L-glutathione and experienced adverse events due to potentially high levels of endotoxins, a substance that may cause unintended health consequences ranging from fever to death.
excerpts.source: FDA, concerns with using dietary ingredient glutathione to compound sterile injectables

excerpts.quote: Postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias.
excerpts.source: Metformin hydrochloride tablets label, boxed warning, DailyMed

excerpts.quote: FDA did not evaluate the proposed uses: insulin resistance, obesity, osteoporosis, vascular calcification, muscle/fat metabolism, longevity because the nomination did not include sufficient information for the Agency to evaluate whether the substance is appropriate for these uses in compounded drug products. In addition, FDA did not identify clinical studies evaluating these uses of MOTS-c.
excerpts.source: FDA briefing on MOTS-c, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee
excerpts.note: This is FDA’s own briefing to its advisers.

excerpts.quote: After conducting a literature search, three studies were found in which epitalon was administered to humans.
excerpts.source: FDA briefing on epitalon, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee
excerpts.note: FDA found none that assessed its safety.

excerpts.quote: Among patients with early Parkinson disease, nicotinamide riboside treatment for 52 weeks did not improve clinical outcomes and was associated with worse clinical outcomes than placebo.
excerpts.note: 410 people in Norway, NR by mouth.

excerpts.quote: While studies have documented the efficacy of some NAD+ precursors such as nicotinamide riboside (NR) in raising plasma NAD+, no data are currently available on the fate of directly infused NAD+ in a human cohort.
excerpts.source: Grant et al., Front Aging Neurosci
excerpts.note: This was the background to their 11-man pilot study of IV NAD+.
